end.summary:
Aarav ordered BCE and CE dates on a timeline in 4 of 5 unaided attempts.
They practised decade, century and millennium; all 3 unaided attempts were correct.
Aarav corrected the BCE counting-direction mix-up during the lesson.
They practised calculating the years between 2600 BCE and 2026 CE as 4625 years.
The 2001-to-century question remained unresolved in the final turn.
end.parentNote: Asha practised timeline ordering, BCE/CE year differences, and the meanings of decade, century and millennium. Aarav used the method of counting BCE years backwards and later applied the add-then-subtract-one rule for dates across BCE and CE. The BCE direction mix-up was corrected during the lesson, but they still mixed up 2001 and the 21st century at the end. At home, ask Aarav to place 1 BCE, 1 CE, 1900, 2000 and 2001 on a timeline, then identify each century.
